bounds: For observed ranks mA,mB, one edit changes each by at most one; clip each rank to [0,nRole], convert paired loss, and intersect with unconditional count bounds. Exact and empty-output cases retain exactness. Global budget uses maximum single weighted downward/upward allowance. Both stopping arms use the same math. These bounds can be conservative.
checks: reserved outcome access absent by enumerated read paths
small exhaustive graph edit bounds and independent brute matching
subject/context mismatch, duplicate/reordered answer, invalid proof, missing-output, unknown-family rejection
mutation test that hidden correction contents do not change visible inputs or initial selection
replay every ordered query and stopping checkpoint
costs: Equal unit image counts; timings split preparation, policy, matching/proposal/checking, service and wall. Human preparation, engineering rates, review, integration and human time remain null. No 3x/2x claim from simulated costs.
decision_rule: Stop selection/stopping superiority claims if conventional arms match. Inconclusive product economics absent real costs/workflows. Preserve counterexamples and narrow the next useful experiment; do not consume reserved outcomes to tune.
edit_semantics: At most one insertion, deletion or replacement of an eligible reference rectangle; arbitrary valid geometry, no inferred correspondence. Per-image budget or one global edit across queried answers. Fixed eligibility policy; not changes to metric or predictions.
exposure: Only the 64 previously exposed REC-D development .boxes.json files. Do not read source correction CSV/pickle or any of the 1433 reserved outcomes. Not preregistered or held out.
membership: 64 singleton images in retained development order; 16 contiguous blocks of four; all-64 including six blocked; linked-58 cohort admitted solely by input availability. Never pool dependent case groups as independent revisions.
no_expansion: No Engine algorithm or limit change, deployment, outreach, paid service, publication, main update or Gate A acceptance.
observations: One whole-image publisher corrected-set answer. Simulated access to actual published corrections, no measured human observation. Separate worker sees visible input and queried answers only; no hidden alternatives, sizes or digests.
question: Do realistic whole-image reference observations support fewer justified queries than conventional baselines, and can residual annotation error make those observations insufficient?

selection.prior_margin: target sign from original-reference total delta (>0 positive; else nonpositive); largest count radius + target sign * original-reference delta, ties by width then development order; fixed per case, never corrected values
selection.width: largest initial count-interval width, ties by development order

stopping: Strict improvement delta=L_A-L_B>0; excluded if upper<=0; unresolved otherwise. Query until decisive, every nonzero-width eligible image is queried, or resource failure. No precision upgrades or repeat observations in this instrument.
uncertainty: Before each whole-image query the reference set is unrestricted, including arbitrary missing/changed boxes. Published original references are ranking hints only. Fixed outputs and metric.
witness_search: After fixed arms finish, recompute nominal full-reference outcomes for all linked cases. Search one-edit geometric counterexamples using deletions and inserting/replacing with each distinct output rectangle in deterministic order. Every candidate uses independent flow; retain first maximum positive and minimum negative effect per image and native-check selected witnesses. Opposite strict decisions in two admitted worlds prove insufficiency; no witness means only bounded-search failure.
